Business.title: French borrowing costs hit 24-year high as civil unrest and budget fears spook markets
Business.text:
France’s borrowing costs have climbed above 5% for the first time in 24 years as political concerns and the government’s failure to agree a much-delayed budget spook the financial markets.

With some civic buildings still smouldering from recent riots, a fresh bout of selling pushed up the yield – or interest rate – on bonds issued by the second largest economy in the eurozone.

The yield on the benchmark 10-year bond – known as obligation assimilables du Trésor (Oat), issued by the French Treasury – rose more than 8 basis points to 5% in morning trading, before easing to 4.99%.

The French government has yet to pass its budget for next year, while the country has been rocked by increasingly violent street protests in recent weeks.

Protests that began in September with students calling for extra funds to deal with mould- and rat-infested schools, a lack of teachers and large class sizes evolved into wider demonstrations about the rising cost of living.

Initially calm protests have often been met with aggressive police tactics, sparking riots in many towns and cities. Stores such as Louis Vuitton have been hit by looting, while protesters set fire to the town hall in Limoges.

No single party has had overall control of parliament since the French president, Emmanuel Macron, called a snap election in 2024. The parliamentary gridlock has blocked his plans to increase the pension age from 62 to 64 and a series of measures designed to reduce or redirect state spending.

France’s budget deficit was 5.1% of gross domestic product in 2025, while its debt pile stood at 115.6% of GDP. Forecasts for the deficit and debt show both increasing in the current financial year without remedial action.

International lenders have become increasingly reticent about lending to Paris, accusing the government of becoming “fiscally incontinent”. Some have withdrawn from lending to France, notably Japanese fund managers, and those that remain have demanded a higher price for their loans, especially longer-period loans.

Matthew Ryan, the head of market strategy at the currency trading and payments platform Ebury, said French woes were also dragging down the value of the euro against other major currencies.

“The euro continues to lag most major currencies as the political risk premium in France looks unlikely to fade any time soon,” he said. “It remains unclear whether the 2027 budget will clear parliament, and even if it does, it seems set to be so riddled with concessions to both the left and the right that the deficit problem is left insufficiently addressed.”

Business.title: Tesla and SpaceX explore merger as Elon Musk gives backing
Business.text:
As SpaceX released its second-ever public earnings report on Tuesday, Elon Musk declared his support for combining the aerospace and AI company with his electric vehicle company, Tesla. He said both companies had created special committees to explore a potential merger, but have not reached any agreement on terms of a transaction.

“Both SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees to discuss this idea at the request of shareholders and these special committees are, uh, consist of independent directors,” Musk said on the call. “Because I’m a conflicted party, I can’t actually be in the discussions of the special committees.”

Musk also expressed his backing for the move, while cautioning about the hurdles involved achieve it. He stated that it would require the approval of 50% of all Tesla shareholders.

“I think some people out there assume that a SpaceX and Tesla merger is a certainty and I think that would be overstating it,” Musk said, adding it would require shareholder approvals and special committees at both firms. “I do think there’s a lot of merit to combining the companies.”

The company revealed a far better financial quarter than Wall Street projected. SpaceX company, which encompasses rockets, artificial intelligence and satellite communications, reported a 161% growth in revenue year over year, driven by its Starlink and AI segments.

The company declared $14.58bn in revenue against analysts’ projected $12.72bn. SpaceX reported earnings per share of 35 cents and a net income of $4.4bn. The company’s stock, which started the day down about 8% for the year, shot up 2% in after hours trading immediately after the results.

Musk appeared alongside SpaceX’s president, Gwynne Shotwell, and CFO, Bret Johnsen, at his Starlink factory in Texas to deliver the earnings report, touting the company’s growth and plans for future rocket developments. Musk also highlighted its artificial intelligence segment, which the company refers to as Super Intelligence, that drew $7.6bn in revenue and now outperforms its Connectivity business, which provides internet services.

Musk’s company once again found itself in the spotlight in recent weeks as investors have speculated about the potential merger with Tesla, the second-most valuable part of the tech mogul’s empire. Musk has also been at the center of geopolitical tensions after Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Ukraine’s president, last week accused SpaceX of restricting access to its military-grade Starlink internet service.

The disruption in service to Starshield allegedly led to several failed Ukrainian combat missions and left the country more vulnerable to Russian drone attacks, as well as highlighted how global internet infrastructure has come to rely on Musk’s products. Musk denied responsibility for the disruption, stating that Starshield was controlled by the US government, not SpaceX. The White House has likewise denied hobbling Starshield.

Moments before the SpaceX earnings call on Tuesday, the Wall Street Journal reported that Musk personally ordered the throttling of Starshield, citing unnamed US officials and people familiar with the matter. Musk faced no questions about the reports on the investor Q&A portion of SpaceX’s earnings call.

While SpaceX’s role in international affairs faces scrutiny, Musk has taken on a resurgent role in US domestic politics. The world’s richest person has contributed $366m in political spending this election cycle, backing Republican-aligned Super Pacs and pouring money into influencing key midterm races. Musk also agreed earlier this month to co-lead a Pentagon project on the future of warfare, bringing him back into government work after his time as the de facto leader of the so-called “department of government efficiency” (Doge).

Musk recently pledged to give every child in the US one of his SpaceX stocks next year, which Donald Trump stated would be facilitated through the president’s “Trump accounts” initiative that creates savings plans for children. The prospective share giveaway is a rare display of philanthropy from Musk, who has criticized traditional aid organizations and has taken credit for dismantling the world’s largest single provider of humanitarian aid by gutting the government agency USAID.

“Giving shares, which are stakes in the future economy, directly to the people is the way,” Musk posted on X, the social media company he owns.

Tech leaders such as Musk have faced increasing public pushback over their extraordinary accumulation of wealth and power in the US, while this year AI firms OpenAI and Anthropic both announced big investments to their grant-making and non-profit arms. Musk’s announcement came after Anthropic announced earlier this week that it plans to donate 5% of its shares to a newly created public benefit fund within the company.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes to remain Man Utd captain despite outburst
Sports.text:
Bruno Fernandes will remain as Manchester United captain and will not be disciplined for his post-match criticism of Michael Carrick after the 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como.

The United skipper criticised Carrick's tactics for the game, then said it was up to the United head coach and his backroom team, not the players, to spot any issues and change them.

It was seen by many externally as a challenge to Carrick's authority, just eight days after United defender Lisandro Martinez criticised director of football Jason Wilcox and the club's summer recruitment.

Inside Old Trafford, there is sympathy for Fernandes for the position he found himself in.

The Portugal midfielder did 10 post-match interviews in Como, despite being replaced by Joshua Zirkzee midway through the second half.

While there is disappointment at some of his comments, it is acknowledged Fernandes' annoyance was understandable given the manner of the loss, which was one of the worst in United's European history.

It remains to be seen whether Fernandes will be picked for Sunday's Premier League encounter with Bournemouth at Old Trafford. Carrick will be asked about the situation when he holds his pre-game news conference at 13:30 BST on Friday.

More to follow.

Sports.title: Felix Balshaw: How the son of an English rugby legend represents France
Sports.text:
Accents quickly reveal a lot about a person.

So speaking to Leeds-born Felix Balshaw - the 20-year-old son of England Rugby World Cup winner Iain - it quickly becomes clear why he is representing France on his climb up the professional tennis ladder.

There is no mistaking a strong Gallic twang as Balshaw, who celebrated the first ATP Tour victory of his career this week, discusses his journey.

Balshaw was born in West Yorkshire while his father played for Premiership club Leeds Tykes, before the family moved to Biarritz when Iain - an electrifying full-back/wing who scored three tries in England's iconic 2003 campaign - joined the cross-channel exodus to the French Top 14.

The Balshaws have remained in the luxurious Basque coastal city, known for its Belle Epoque architecture, Atlantic seafront casinos and world-class surfing.

"We came down in Biarritz in 2009 and we just loved the place," said Felix, who broke into the world's top 200 last month for the first time.

"I grew up in France and, as each day went by, I felt more and more French.

"Since I've been little, from when I started playing in Tennis Europe juniors, I have always had the French flag by my name."

Balshaw pledging allegiance to his adopted country is understandable given his limited contact with his birthland.

Trips back across the English Channel have been "very rare" for the Balshaw children, largely restricted to Christmas family gatherings.

Their maternal grandmother lives in Bath, although Felix has never visited his father's hometown of Blackburn.

But the world number 178 is fully aware his dad will forever be ingrained in the fabric of English sporting history.

The then Bath player scored three tries during England's historic 2003 World Cup campaign, helping secure a 20-17 victory over Australia in the final when he came on as a second-half substitute.

On the eve of the biggest match of his career - facing fellow Frenchman Corentin Moutet in the Lyon Open second round - Felix tried to draw inspiration from watching highlights of his father playing in 2003.

"I just had a massive smile [watching] because I can say 'this is my dad'," he said.

"When he was at Biarritz I was always stood in a little corner in the stands with the rugby gang. It was very, very inspirational to watch him.

"As a father he's tough, but it's always important that he has a lot of experience in rugby, so he's got a lot of stuff to teach me.

"He's always been a great, great part of my life. He's always had my back."

Balshaw started playing tennis at the age of four, but unsurprisingly also had a talent for rugby.

At 13, he needed to make a choice about which sport he wanted to pursue more seriously with the prospect of a professional career looming.

"When I was little, and your father is a rugby champion, of course you always want to follow in his steps and do the same journey as him," Balshaw said.

"But I just felt that rugby was not going to be my sport.

"Tennis, I guess, is more difficult for me than rugby because it's an individual sport, but there was a little more fire in me [playing tennis].

"That meant it was the right choice to choose tennis."

Balshaw is essentially an inverted Arthur Fery - the French-born British number one who became a household name with a stunning run to the Wimbledon semi-finals in July.

The pair actually met for the first time at this week's ATP 250 event in Lyon, where Balshaw beat Portuguese world number 56 Jaime Faria for his maiden win at tour level.

Possessing a Roger Federer-style one-handed backhand, and a Thor-inspired hammer celebration, Balshaw announced his arrival in some style.

Next week Balshaw will rise into the world's top 180, having starting the 2026 season ranked 718th.

His success will also attract interest among Lawn Tennis Association (LTA) chiefs, who are desperate to increase the pool of British players at the elite level.

Was Balshaw ever approached by the LTA to represent the country of his birth?

And was there ever a conversation with his parents about who he should represent?

"Maybe my parents are hiding stuff and I don't know, but I have never been personally contacted by the LTA," Felix said.

"I think for [my parents] the most important thing is if I'm happy, they'll be happy as well."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick: Man Utd boss carrying on as Old Trafford club eyes possible replacements
Sports.text:
Michael Carrick is set to remain in charge of Manchester United for Sunday's Premier League match against Bournemouth, but senior figures are concerned about performances and results.

Carrick is said to be carrying on as normal and has not been made aware of any imminent change following Wednesday's humiliating 4-1 defeat by Italian side Como.

But some at Old Trafford believe the squad should be doing much better, with one source telling BBC Sport: "We need to work hard to get through it."

Another accepted the level of current injuries "doesn't help, but no excuse", claiming effort levels were "concerning".

"We have a Champions League squad and need to be playing at that level," the source said.

Despite concern at the performances, some in the United hierachy are of the view chopping and changing mangers so regularly in recent years has failed to arrest United's decline, and Carrick has been let down by players who are under-performing.

While club sources say Carrick will remain in charge for Sunday's match, United have already begun the process of identifying possible replacements.

Eddie Howe, Antonio Conte and Julian Nagelsmann are understood to have their eyes on the Old Trafford job.

After Wednesday's match - United's seventh in a row without a win - captain Bruno Fernandes questioned Carrick's tactics.

The players were given Thursday off but will be back at Carrington on Friday when Carrick will hold his news conference to preview the Bournemouth match at 1330 BST.

While there remains major uncertainty over Carrick future, there is also an appreciation in some quarters of the progress he and his squad made last season, and a view he should be given more time to turn things around.

For weeks, managers - in and out of work - have grown aware the United job may become available.

Howe, for example, is available and would be considered. Sources have indicated the former Newcastle boss is open to returning to management with United after leaving St James' Park in the close season.

Former Chelsea boss Conte and ex-Germany manager Naglesmann, who are also out of work, are also interested.

Aston Villa head coach Unai Emery and Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler's stock is high with those in the corridors of power at United - but extracting them from their respective clubs would be difficult.

For the third year in a row, United have publicly and financially backed a manager in the summer, but positive results have not followed.

Ruben Amorim staggered on to January, but the shock League Cup defeat at League Two side Grimsby last August and the awful performance at Brentford less than a month later stripped away his safety net and gave United's hierarchy nowhere to go when he attacked their influence.

United looked extensively at other candidates, including Thomas Tuchel and Roberto de Zerbi, in the summer of 2024 before deciding to stick with Erik ten Hag. The Dutchman was dismissed in the October.

Now, we have Carrick.

There were dissenting voices when he was appointed on a permanent basis in May, but the majority of supporters felt 12 wins from 17 in interim charge and a place in the Champions League after a two-year absence meant the 45-year-old former United midfielder deserved a crack at the job.

But, as ever, results shape everything.

There are numerous reasons behind the club's poor form this season and blame can be apportioned across a variety of departments and to the very top of the club.

However, the brutal truth is two wins from 11 games, and none in seven, their worst run since 2015-16 when eight matches without a win took Louis van Gaal to the brink of dismissal, is simply not good enough. And as head coach, Carrick bears significant responsibility for that.

Accusations of a lack of passion, desire and intensity have dogged United all season, having won just two of their matches in all competitions.

The team have also been hampered by injuries and players failing to reach the level anticipated.

While they have struggled in attack, they have also only kept a single clean sheet all season as form, results and confidence have all dipped.

Mixed into that negativity has come explosive post-match comments from experienced defender Lisandro Martinez, attacking the recruitment, and Fernandes, attacking Carrick and his tactics.

In between was the interview in the Athletic with Ten Hag when he spoke of 'broken promises' and a 'toxic culture'. It all smacks of a club lacking control, discipline and a clear forward-looking strategy.

There is certainly a view from senior figures around the club that while overall recruitment can be questioned - specifically strengthening midfield in the summer at the expense of bringing in striking support for Benjamin Sesko or competition at left-back - the players have to take a significant amount of responsibility.

Whether that helps Carrick is another matter.

The proximity of United's next Premier League game does not make immediate change straightforward, even if that was the thinking.

Following Amorim's dismissal in January, former United midfielder Darren Fletcher took over as interim manager for two games. Fletcher subsequently returned to his role as Under-18 coach, but two of the coaches who helped him, Jonny Evans and Travis Binnion, stayed with the senior set-up as part of Carrick's team.

United have a clear midweek coming up following their EFL Cup defeat by Brighton, who came back from two down to win at Old Trafford last month. That, in theory, would allow time to take stock without the immediate pressure a match can bring.

Bournemouth secured their first Premier League win under new boss Marco Rose last week. They drew 4-4 in a memorable encounter at Old Trafford last season, prior to that, they won 3-0 on both of their previous two visits.

It remains to be seen if Carrick will be in charge, and if so, how long after that.

It seems the only certainty around Manchester United just now, is the sense of uncertainty - again.

Sports.title: Sri Lanka chase 430 to beat England despite Harry Brook 202
Sports.text:
One-day international tri-series, Rawalpindi

England 429-4 (50 overs): Brook 202, Root 69, Jacks 66*

Sri Lanka 430-8 (49.5 overs): Rathnayake 130, Avishka 97, Shanaka 97

Sri Lanka won by two wickets

Harry Brook's first double century by an England batter in a one-day international was not enough to prevent his team being stunned by Sri Lanka, who pulled off a remarkable chase of 430 in Rawalpindi.

Brook passed Ben Stokes' previous England best score of 182 and posted the fastest ODI double hundred, off 114 balls, in his astonishing 202.

In clobbering the 14th double-hundred in a men's one-day international and the 12th highest individual score, Brook lifted England to 429-4 – at halfway the highest total made in a one-day international in Pakistan.

But Sri Lanka, who chose to bat second, were not deterred, even when they were reduced to 24-2. They set about completing the second-highest successful chase in ODI history.

Pavan Rathnayake made a sublime 130, while Aviksha Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both added 97.

With Jofra Archer rested for the tri-series and leg-spinner Adil Rashid left out of this match for tactical reasons, England's bowling was woeful. Sam Curran conceded 103 runs from his nine overs.

Up with the required rate throughout their innings, Sri Lanka needed 109 from the final 10 overs and were able to absorb the losses of Rathnayake and Shanaka.

Sri Lanka needed eight off the final over, sent down by Josh Tongue, who was pinpoint with his accuracy to bowl Dinuth Wellalage and Eshan Malinga with successive deliveries.

But in a sensational finish, Janith Liyanage, the man bowling when Brook reached 200, would not be denied.

With six needed from two balls, Liyanage pummelled Tongue's penultimate delivery of the match down the ground for a match-winning maximum, sparking joyous of celebrations by the Sri Lankans.

One of the most incredible one-day internationals ever played ended with an aggregate of 847 runs, behind only a match total of 872 when South Africa chased 435 to beat Australia in 2006.

The total of 123 boundaries across both innings - 93 fours and 30 sixes - is also a record in ODIs.

How did England lose this game? At halfway, when Brook left the field arm-in-arm with Will Jacks, the thought of Sri Lanka even getting close to their target seemed highly fanciful.

Yet, Sri Lankan captain Kusal Mendis' decision to chase proved inspired, despite the way his team were dismantled by Brook.

Ultimately, Sri Lanka put the conditions – and Brook's knock – into context, helped by an England team who wilted under the pressure.

They were hampered by the dew, another factor in Sri Lanka's decision to bat second. England made mistakes in the field and their bowlers struggled to grip the ball. Without Archer, they lacked a death bowler.

And, with less then a year to go until the World Cup, England showed no composure as the game began to run away from them.

For as well as Brook batted, his tactics will come into question. Too much faith was placed in Curran, whose 103-2 are the most expensive figures returned by an England bowler in an ODI.

Gus Atkinson opened the bowling and sent down just seven overs of his allotted 10 and Tongue, who almost rescued the game, was only into his ninth.

This tri-series is designed to replicate the tournament conditions England will face at the World Cup in southern Africa. Two games in they are without a win and facing the prospect of needing to beat Pakistan in Lahore on Sunday to stay in the competition.

Sports.title: South Africa vs Australia: Hosts win by an innings and 31 runs to level series
Sports.text:
Second Test, Gqeberha (day five of five)

South Africa 425-9 dec: Bavuma 179, Jansen 85; Boland 5-81

Australia 99 & 295: Head 121; Rabada 4-77, Mulder 3-64

South Africa won by an innings and 31 runs

South Africa broke Australia's resistance in the final session to complete a famous victory in the second Test and set up a series decider in Cape Town.

Travis Head made 121 for Australia and Scott Boland survived 166 deliveries for 40 runs in an attempt to escape Gqeberha with a draw - the tourists' hopes also boosted by the first session being wiped out by rain.

But the Proteas stuck to their task to take the six wickets needed to win by an innings and 31 runs as the light faded late on the last day.

Premier paceman Kagiso Rabada finished with 4-77 while Marco Jansen, whose 5-33 on day four put South Africa in the ascendancy, took the final wicket as Australia were dismissed for 295.

But all-rounder Wiaan Mulder also played a crucial hand, bowling with accuracy and finding movement off the pitch to dismiss Head, Boland and Australia captain Pat Cummins.

Some of South Africa's great Test wins have come against Australia - notably in the last World Test Championship final two years ago and a Test on this ground in 2018 in the infamous Sandpaper series. This must surely rank highly among them.

They were heavily beaten in the first Test in Durban and when 40-4 and 110-6 in their first innings of this Test, there appeared only one winner in this series.

Instead, the contest has been turned on its head by Bavuma's epic 179 and South Africa twice dismissing Australia, setting up a tantalising finale in Cape Town.

The third Test begins on Tuesday.

Sports.title: Jordan Elliott: Defensive tackle released by Tenessee Titans after pulling gun in car park
Sports.text:
Defensive tackle Jordan Elliott has been released by the Tennessee Titans after he pulled a gun in the car park of the team facility.

Titans coach Robert Saleh confirmed on Tuesday reports that Elliott retrieved a gun from his car after an altercation with JC Latham during practice on 15 October.

The 28-year-old did not play in Sunday's victory against the Indianapolis Colts and was released by the Titans on Tuesday over what the club called an "incident".

"Just pause with regards to the news that Jordan had a gun," Saleh said.

"This is a man who is a father, a great husband. This is a man who has never committed a crime in his entire life.

"And he pulled a gun in the parking lot. Why did he go off the rails and grab a gun? To me, those are small signs of a cry for help. Obviously there is something greater happening."

Offensive tackle Latham called the altercation with Elliott an "unfortunate situation" that happened "just in the heat of the moment".

"Never been no bad blood between us two. We never actually had an argument leading up to it," Latham said.

"I do think mental health is extremely important and that's just one of those situations where you pray for a guy like that and, if you can, reach out to him, hope for the best for him. It's nothing personal on my end."

Elliott, who previously played for San Francisco and Cleveland, has appeared in five games this season.

Saleh said he would still recommend Elliott to another franchise.

"My message to 31 other teams would be if you need a hell of a run-stopping D-tackle that can help you on a play-off run, give me a call, I'll tell you everything you need to know about him," he said.

"I will stand on the table for Jordan's character. Unfortunately rules are rules with regards to guns on property, and sometimes it's far greater than the knee-jerk reaction of kicking somebody when they're down."

Sports.title: Tour de France 2027 UK stages in detail: Where will you stand?
Sports.text:
The street-by-street details for the six British-based stages that will start both the men's and women's editions of the 2027 Tour de France have been revealed.

The three-week men's race gets under way with a stage from Edinburgh to Carlisle on 2 July. It is followed by a route between Keswick and Liverpool before Wales hosts a third and final grand depart stage from Welshpool to Cardiff on 4 July.

The women's event starts on 30 July with a race from Leeds to Manchester, before moving back across the Pennines to Yorkshire with a finish in Sheffield.

A testing team time trial around the streets of central London will complete the opening section of that nine-stage race.

The collaboration is a first for both races in a Super Grand Depart - the finer details of which were announced at a ceremony hosted by the Tour's organisers ASO on Paris' Palais de Congres on Thursday.

Men's race director Christian Prudhomme added: "Just a few weeks apart, the Tour de France and the Tour de France Femmes avec Zwift will each take their respective pelotons on a journey through the roads of the United Kingdom.

"Along with what we anticipate will be a warm and massive welcome for the champions, Great Britain also offers us a symbol that further ties the two races together. From the start on 2 July at the foot of Edinburgh Castle, which will be the northernmost in the history of the Tour, to a team time trial in London on 1 August.

"Needless to say, there will be thousands of thrills and emotions."

Stages of the Tour have been held in the UK before, in 1974, 1994 and 2007 in London and the Yorkshire Grand Depart in 2014.

This will be the first time both men's and women's events have come to the same nation outside France in the same year.

Sports.title: Welcome to the trap: swaggering Atlanta Dream turn WNBA finals into a hometown spectacle
Sports.text:
The Atlanta Dream were exactly where they wanted to be on Wednesday night, comfortably ensconced inside their downtown arena for Game 3 of the WNBA finals against the Golden State Valkyries. Kerry Washington, Ludacris and Cam Newton led the courtside celebrity delegation. Quavo and TI headlined the half-time show, while two more hugely popular Atlanta rappers performed during other extended play stoppages – a mini-spectacle that speaks to the city’s deep bench of hip-hop talent.

But it was the crowd that really made State Farm Arena a house of horrors for Golden State. They didn’t just fill the 17,608-seat venue. They donned matching sky-blue T-shirts and waved rally towels. They sang along with their favorite emcees and lived and died with every point. They were so loud in the first quarter that I couldn’t hear the referee’s whistle from my 100-level press seat. They stayed to the end – well, two minutes from the buzzer anyway (gotta beat traffic) – and, with the 97-71 win sealed and DJ Khaled’s All I Do Is Win blasting through the arena speakers, serenaded the departing Valkyries with the unofficial Atlanta battle cry: “ATL hoe!”

Angel Reese never knew basketball could be like this. “When you can have at the end of the quarter a performance,” she gushed after a 21-point, 12-rebound effort. “And at the timeout, another performance. You smell the chicken, you smell the fish. It’s a blue-out in here. I didn’t even get to see Kerry. You don’t know who you gonna see in the A.”

Atlanta has always been a strange sports town – one where fans learn not to fall too hard, lest they get burned by teams that either get ahead of themselves, self-destruct or wear out your patience with their underachievment. So fans proceed with apprehension. They find out-of-town teams to insulate themselves from disappointment, leave games early when defeat seems imminent and convince themselves they’re just beating traffic. They enjoy the music, the invitations to sing along and swag surf.

The last time a playoff basketball game was played at State Farm Arena, the Knicks routed the Hawks to seal their Eastern Conference first-round series – and by the end, the New York fans had cleared out most of the Atlanta supporters and glitterati. With the Hawks down some 40 points, rappers Young Joc and Lil Boosie performed their hits for a crowd that half-bobbed along. It was hard to imagine the Atlanta sports scene getting more unserious.

Then the Dream reached the WNBA finals, only to learn they wouldn’t be able to play at State Farm Arena – their occasional home court. The Hawks, State Farm’s main tenant, were opening their season, while emo-pop artist Sombr had a gig scheduled. The Dream faced the possibility of hosting their first WNBA finals game in 13 years at the 3,500-seat airport arena where they played most of their home games, with neither the local college arenas nor the 13,000-seat suburban concert venue available. Gateway would have made for a jarring contrast with Chase Center – the NBA arena where the Valkyries’ passionate, violet-clad fans have created Ballhalla, one of the WNBA’s toughest places to play. The racial and economic makeup of the Atlanta and Golden State crowds would have surely added another dimension. But a combined effort by the teams, the league and the arena to bring the games to State Farm spared us that discourse.

It allowed Dream fans to show they can match that home-court advantage when Atlanta has a team worth believing in and the right venue. Three previous times the Dream have reached the finals, only for all three appearances to end in sweeps. But no one was thinking much about that on Wednesday night. Not with the Dream holding the Valkyries scoreless for the first five minutes before picking up where they left off in Game 2 and smothering them with their defense. Not with Reese jawing at the Valkyries bench after tough layups and, for good measure, setting off the crowd with a pair of open threes as her college coach, LSU’s Kim Mulkey, looked on in her blued-out pantsuit. Not with the Dream’s length and speed throwing a spanner into the Valkyries’ carefully choreographed offense, forcing Golden State to heave away at the basket late in the shot clock.

Only thanks to three-point shooting from Cecilia Zandalasini and Gabby Williams did Golden State cut the deficit to six by half-time, then pulled level at 48 in the third quarter, with Zandalasini perfect beyond the arc to that point. Otherwise, a Valkyries team that prides itself on depth and balance was mostly caught off guard by a Dream team beating them at their own game while also doing what they do best: short-circuiting the pick-and-roll, winning extra possessions on steals and rebounds and scoring in transition.

Former No 1 draft pick Rhyne Howard, one of three Dream players named to the WNBA’s all-defensive team last week, became the first player to record five or more steals in consecutive finals games. Reese, the newly crowned defensive player of the year, became the youngest player in WNBA history to record a double-double in three straight finals games and joined A’ja Wilson as the only players to record at least 20 points and 10 rebounds in consecutive finals games. The Valkyries bench was a major factor again, outscoring the Dream reserves 38-27. But that advantage counted for little with Atlanta neutralizing Golden State starters Kiah Stokes, Veronica Burton and Kayla Thornton, who combined for five points on 2-of-11 shooting.

Sports.title: Rookie Lendeborg jaws at ‘weak ass’ Dončić and admits he didn’t watch much NBA
Sports.text:
Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg had an extraordinary NBA debut as he jawed with Luka Dončić and admitted he had largely been exposed to the league through highlights before turning professional.

Lendeborg was given the task of guarding the Los Angeles Lakers star for large parts of Wednesday’s game, which Dončić’s team won 127-105.

However, Lendeborg said he “lost all respect” for Dončić’s quest for foul calls during the game.

“I had a lot of respect for him [because] I didn’t really watch the NBA much,” Lendeborg said. “I just watched highlights and seen him kill people. But being in it firsthand and seeing all the whining and complaining, I lost all respect.”

Lendeborg was the No 11 overall pick by the Warriors in this year’s draft after helping Michigan win the NCAA Tournament. He had early success shutting down Dončić, but the six-time All-Star went on to score 28 points in the Lakers’ victory.

In the second quarter, Dončić was fouled by Lendeborg after a pump fake and celebrated in front of the rookie.

“You get the foul call. Congratulations, bro,” Lendeborg said. “Then you talk to me like you did something great. C’mon, dog. That shit is weak. It kind of threw me off because I have so much respect for him. Gone, man. Gone.”

Lendeborg was given a technical for jawing at Dončić. “I was telling him he sucks,” Lendeborg said. “He can’t score on me. You talk but you can’t score on me. I said it the whole game. I said a couple cuss words, obviously. That’s why I got the technical. But I was letting him know.”

Lendeborg seemed unimpressed by the league in general after his debut.

“I guess this is what the NBA is like, man,” Lendeborg said. “A lot of flopping, a lot of foul baiting, a lot of praying to the refs, man. Interesting first game for me.”

Lendeborg had already made an impression before his debut. He admitted he used to hate his new teammate Stephen Curry because he was a fan of one of his playing rivals, Kyrie Irving. Warriors veteran Draymond Green, who is not shy of expressing his own opinions, had no problems with the rookie’s attitude.

“In this league, everybody always says, ‘Oh, there’s certain guys you got to respect,’” Green said after Wednesday’s game. “I ain’t come in the league like that. Everybody will say, ‘Oh, the rookie learned his lesson.’ What’d he learn? The next time he see him, go at his ass again.”

For his part, Dončić said he was trying to stay out of trouble.

“He was talking crazy,” Dončić said. “But I wasn’t trying to talk back. This season, I’m not trying to get techs.”

Gaming_Tech.title: Barclays cutting 5,000 jobs as it increases reliance on AI
Gaming_Tech.text:
Barclays is cutting around 5,000 staff as it introduces more artificial intelligence (AI) into its work processes.

The banking group said 1,000 posts had already been closed and it expects a further reduction of 4,000 to be complete by the end of this year, amounting to around 5% of its global workforce.

The bank's cost reductions are focused on its UK retail bank, but some back office functions for the UK are done in India, where a significant proportion of the job cuts are expected to fall.

Barclays said the changes were the result of an ongoing modernisation plan, with the use of AI being the "icing on the cake" of its strategy.

Although not all of the cuts are due to AI, their scale will prompt further concern over the impact of the new technology.

Company spending on AI is increasing along with claims new tools can replace some of the basic tasks currently done by staff such as administrative and programming work.

HSBC, Standard Chartered and Danske Bank have also flagged AI-related job cuts this year.

"It is a hot button topic," said AJ Bell investment analyst, Russ Mould.

However, banks had not yet made big moves towards the widespread introduction of AI and they would be considering the implications for security and customer service before implementing AI technology to make financial savings, he said.

"Any company at any time needs to keep on top of its cost base," he said.

"It will be intriguing to see what other banks say in their results in the coming weeks.

Sharon Graham, general secretary of the Unite union that represents banking sector workers said the company was "using AI as an excuse to discard its loyal and long-suffering workforce".

"Employers should be focussed on upgrading employees' skills so that they remain employed as new technology changes the workplace. Instead, Barclays is guilty of taking a short-term, kneejerk approach," she said.

Barclays is reaching the end of a three year cost-cutting programme focused primarily on its UK retail banking arm, although the investment banking division is also affected.

AJ Bell's Russ Mould said despite "reaching for the AI lever" Barclays had failed to match expectations with its financial results.

Barclays also revealed it made £2.3bn profit in the three months to September, higher than the same period a year ago, but slightly less than forecast.

Barclays Group chief executive CS Venkatakrishnan said the job cuts were the result of significant investment it is making in technology to simplify and improve its business.

"AI has an important role to play and may have a more important role to play in the future.

"We will employ the AI at scale," he said. "But AI is the icing on the cake not the cake.

"Because you need to do the infrastructure build to get the benefits of AI."

Barclays said around 60% of the job cuts will fall within its support functions, including among developers.

Will Howlett, financials analyst at Quilter Cheviot said the cuts illustrated "how significantly AI and automation could reshape the banking industry over the next few years".

"Banks have spent heavily on technology for years, but we are increasingly reaching the point where that investment translates into fewer people being required to run the business," he said.

Barclays said it expects its efficiency measures to deliver a further £1.1bn of savings in 2027.

Gaming_Tech.title: Telford Gun Hall opening marks return of tank barrel production to UK
Gaming_Tech.text:
The production of gun barrels to be used on tanks has returned to the UK for the first time in 20 years with the opening of a new manufacturing facility.

The UK Gun Hall in Telford, run by German defence firm Rheinmetall, has supported 100 jobs and will make barrels and breaches for large calibre weapons.

Defence secretary, Wes Streeting, attended the opening ceremony on Thursday and said Britain was "back in the business of making weapons" for its armed forces.

"From an empty site to full production in eight months, this is rapid reindustrialisation in action," he said.

"One hundred skilled jobs in world class manufacturing and the return of large calibre weapon production to UK soil for the first time in 20 years - this is what defence as an engine for growth looks like," Streeting added.

The barrels and breaches will be made for both 120m and 155mm weapon systems, including for the RCH 155 and future artillery platforms, according to Rheinmetall.

Gaming_Tech.title: PHP: What is it and why did it spark a global cyber security scramble?
Gaming_Tech.text:
For more than a decade, serious flaws had gone undetected in the technology underpinning much of the internet.

It took AI to bring them to light and caused a global cyber-security alert.

The vulnerabilities lie within a programming language called PHP, which has been used internationally since the 2000s to build websites.

Governments and cyber-security agencies around the world are scrambling to contain the fallout of the discovery on Wednesday, and have urged website operators to install a new emergency fix or consider taking their platforms offline.

Cyber-security firm Wiz - one of the companies whose researchers uncovered the vulnerabilities - described the flaws as the "most severe" ever detected by AI.

OpenAI, whose technology was used to find the flaws, called the discovery "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory".

Most people may not have heard of PHP, but they probably interact with it daily.

It stands for PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor, an open-source, back-end programming language which runs on a web server.

Developed in the early 1990s to help serve dynamic web pages and applications, PHP still powers lots of platforms today, including Wikipedia, online shops and WordPress – the system behind many websites.

When you visit a site, PHP is the code which collects data and effectively turns it into a page you can read.

It has also been used to write a number of tools for building or speeding up the creation of web apps, with Laravel, Symfony and Drupal among popular PHP frameworks.

According to cyber-security firm Wiz, which helped uncover the critical PHP vulnerabilities surfaced this week, PHP powers 70% of the world's websites.

It is maintained by a non-profit called the PHP Foundation, external, composed of individuals and companies which depend on the language and aim to ensure its "long-term prosperity".

A group of cyber-security researchers and organisations disclosed two vulnerabilities within PHP this week, which they warned could have the potential to upend sites across the internet.

Cyber firms Wiz and Calif said the flaws – coined "php2shell" - were inherent in the language itself, with versions of PHP released over the last decade affected.

Ryan Austin, a Calif researcher who helped uncover the security issues, told the BBC it was "the most serious vulnerability I've ever found".

Wiz wrote in a blog post, external about its findings that, under the right conditions, hackers could exploit the php2shell issue to take control of affected web servers and steal sensitive data - saying everything built on PHP was left exposed.

AI could also make such attacks easier and faster, Paul Spain, chief executive of Gorilla Cyber Security, told the BBC.

He estimated the flaw could affect "millions and millions" of websites.

Jill Slay, a cyber-security researcher at the University of Adelaide, said it would be "disastrous" if hackers or countries weaponised the flaw and seized private data from websites.

The PHP Foundation rolled out patches on Wednesday to fix the vulnerabilities that had been lurking in their software for years.

"All PHP users are strongly encouraged to update immediately," the company said.

Authorities and security organisations around the world have echoed those warnings to website operators to secure their platforms.

The US National Security Agency told all organisations that use PHP to take their systems offline if they were unable to patch them immediately, adding that the flaw could provide a "direct path" to exploit a system's database.

"These risks are serious enough to require immediate patching across United States Government departments and agencies," the agency said.

The UK's National Cyber Security Centre gave similar advice and told organisations to check for "backdoors installed by an attacker".

Its counterparts in the EU, Singapore and Australia have also issued similar alerts.

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi urged people to check if their publicly available websites ran on PHP.

"We have an urgent request for everyone to take action tonight," Takaichi wrote on X.

"If it is difficult to apply the fix patch promptly, temporarily suspending websites and similar measures can be considered an effective way to reduce risk," she said.

Tech companies have also sought to quickly secure their systems.

E-commerce giant Amazon said it was targeted in multiple attempts days before the public disclosure of the PHP issue, but its websites were operating as normal.

Matthew Prince, the boss of internet infrastructure firm Cloudflare, also said it had seen "thousands" of attempts to exploit the PHP vulnerabilities across its network in the 10 hours before it was publicly announced.

"That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post announcement, hundreds of thousands within two hours, and millions now," he wrote on X, external.

The issue affects back-end website and web development processes that will be invisible to many users - meaning most people won't need to take any action.

But small businesses with sites, including those built using WordPress, may be wondering how to protect themselves.

Those who own websites or manage infrastructure running PHP have been urged to secure their websites by updating to the latest version.

Ethical hacker Ken Munro, who has spent years finding security flaws in computer systems, says installing the fixes - known as patching - is "a bit like running a Windows update".

If a hosting company or web developer manages your website, contact them and ask whether the PHP security fixes have been applied - something that must be applied to PHP itself and cannot be resolved by updating WordPress or its plugins.

If you look after your website yourself, Munro says "it is your own responsibility to make sure fixes are applied".

The UK's National Cyber Security Centre recommends, external considering temporarily taking sites offline if updates or temporary protections cannot be applied quickly enough.

The US National Security Agency has also urged "heightened awareness" in the coming weeks, telling people to closely monitor updates from software vendors.

"Vigilance in applying patches related to those systems is paramount," it said, external.

And while the onus lies mainly on website operators, users should stay alert for any security advice issued by affected services, such as requests to change passwords, Kanhere said.

He warned people to be alert to any phishing messages exploiting the publicity around the incident too.
Gaming_Tech.description: For more than a decade, serious flaws had gone undetected in the technology underpinning much of the internet. It took AI to bring them to light and caused a global cyber-security alert. The vulnerabilities lie within a programming language called PHP, which has been used internationally since the 2000s to build...

Gaming_Tech.title: Websites taken down worldwide as critical PHP cyber-security update issued
Gaming_Tech.text:
International governments and agencies have urged websites to address two critical cyber-security flaws in a programming language which powers much of the internet.

The vulnerabilities were found within the PHP programming language, with a fix issued on Wednesday afternoon.

Multiple cyber-security agencies have urged organisations unable to apply fixes in time to consider taking their sites down, leading bodies such as the Finnish government, Edinburgh council and the BBC to take pages offline.

The flaws were discovered by AI, with cyber-security firm Wiz saying they were the "most severe vulnerabilities ever discovered" by the tech, which is reshaping the cyber landscape.

Finland has temporarily shut down the government's public web services, while the Netherlands' cyber-security agency said it was taking its own website offline due to the vulnerabilities.

The US National Security Agency issued similar advice on X, external for organisations to take their systems offline if they were unable to update with the fix.

"These vulnerabilities often provide a direct path to the server's file system or database," it wrote.

Meanwhile, the White House said federal agencies were working with leading AI labs to speed up a fix to the issue.

And in a post on X, external, Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi urged people to check if their publicly available websites ran on PHP.

The Wikimedia Foundation, which runs the online encyclopedia Wikipedia, said it was addressing the security vulnerabilities.

"We have taken down a number of other systems as a precautionary measure until they can be safely patched," it said.

That led some people to be unable to access parts of Wikipedia on Wednesday.

Edinburgh council's website has also become inaccessible, as well as the online homes for several BBC programmes including Doctor Who and The Traitors.

They have not confirmed a link to PHP - BBC News has approached them for comment.

Other websites, including the art platform DeviantArt, have said they are "temporarily down for maintenance, external" without specifying the reason.

The vulnerabilities were discovered by cyber-security researchers at the firms Calif and Wiz.

Calif, along with PHP Foundation, were part of a program started by OpenAI called Patch the Planet.

Through that program, they were given access to the AI company's advanced AI tools in order to find and fix flaws in web development language.

OpenAI said in a blog post, external that the discovery was "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory". It added an internal researcher at the company had also discovered the issue around the same time as the other firms.

The flaws had gone undetected for more than a decade. By August, after a few weeks of using advanced AI tools, they were discovered.

"Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours," Wiz said in a blog post.

It has estimated "roughly 70%" of the internet is affected, though the BBC is unable to verify that figure.

While PHP Foundation intended to release its discovery later this month along with a complete fix for the problem, usually referred to by software developers as a "patch," details of the flaw were leaked on social media on Tuesday.

It forced PHP Foundation to rush out its announcement of the vulnerability and its huge scale.

The Netherlands' National Institute for Public Health and the Environment, an agency of the Dutch government, has taken down its website.

Similarly the website of the Tweede Kamer, the lower house of the nation's parliament, has become inaccessible.

The UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), as well as its counterparts in the EU and Australia have urged those who use PHP to apply the fixes.

"Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated," the NCSC said in a note, external.

Japan's national cyber-security office and EU cyber-security officials have issued a similar warning, external.

"PHP is everywhere. It ​quietly powers WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful ⁠lot of software that doesn't even advertise that it runs PHP under the hood," cyber-security company Huntress said.

Cyber-security expert Don Smith, from the Sophos Counter Threat Unit, told the BBC this would "likely be a priority target" for hackers.

The immediate challenge was not simply installing a patch to fix the issue, but finding and managing every instance where PHP was running, he said.

"The use of PHP is pervasive, it can sit beneath public websites, content management systems, hosting platforms and third-party products, sometimes without even being obvious to the organisation using it," he said.

He said it was crucial that organisations looked out for signs that an attacker "might have already have gained a foothold".

The European Union Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-EU) said the risk scores given to the vulnerabilities "indicate the potential for unauthenticated remote code execution".

Such a cyber-attack could potentially allow hackers to install malware and take down websites.

Dane Knecht, chief technology officer at internet infrastructure firm Cloudflare, said he was, external "seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up".

The NCSC said once organisations have installed the update, they should "continuously monitor for security updates from third-party software vendors, including for appliances and services that may bundle PHP".

It is not yet clear which versions of the programming language are affected, but CERT-EU said it could affect all versions of it dating back to PHP 5 onwards - which launched in 2004.

The PHP Foundation has issued the update only for the latest versions however - with people using PHP 8.1 or older being urged to upgrade.

PHP was created for web development. It is used on servers to implement what you see when you visit websites.

Not all websites use it, but it nonetheless powers a large portion of the internet.

Gaming_Tech.title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy
Gaming_Tech.text:
Meta, the company behind Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp has been hit with its largest fine ever for its business practices.

A judge in New Mexico on Wednesday ordered the company to pay $25bn (£18.6bn) following a two-week trial earlier this year that found it had spent years lying to the public about how it handled Facebook user data.

"The lies extend beyond Facebook's data practices as well," the judge said, adding they went to "the heart of Facebook's core business practices".

Meta's head lawyer CJ Mahoney said the ruling made it "all but impossible to do business in the state of New Mexico". The company intends to appeal, a move Mahoney said will be successful.

The fine is the largest to date against Meta, which has either been fined or agreed to settle several other lawsuits this year, including an $18bn deal with California over child safety.

New Mexico's lawsuit stemmed from the role of Meta, then still doing business as Facebook, in what became known as the Cambridge Analytica scandal.

That firm utilised data and information from millions of Facebook users as part of its work in political consulting, including on work related to the 2016 US Presidential election, which saw Donald Trump elected for the first time.

New Mexico had also accused Meta of intentionally misleading the public on how it benefitted from content that included hate speech, and how such rules against it were enforced. The jury found the company had intentionally misled the public on those claims, too.

Meta disputed those accusations. "At its core, this lawsuit seeks to impose a tax on speech to enforce new rules for what people can say online," Mahoney added.

Lawyers for New Mexico sued the company over many statements Meta executives had made over the years that user data was never shared with or accessed by third parties without a user's permission, when in reality it had been.

They claimed that the entire population of the state, roughly two million people, was impacted by Meta's dishonesty regarding the way it controlled user data. A jury found that Meta had violated state laws more than 40 million times.

"For too long, powerful technology companies have operated as though their size and influence put them beyond the reach of the law," New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez said on Wednesday.

"Today's result makes clear that no corporation is too powerful to be held accountable."

The state lawyers sought up to $40bn in fines against Meta. Meta had argued anything beyond $3.4bn would be unconstitutional.

Judge Francis Mathew on Wednesday was direct in his decision to fine Meta an amount roughly equal to its profits each quarter.

He said Meta's violations of law and misrepresentations to the public about how their Facebook data was used and shared were "willful" and spanned "more than 11 years", stretching from 2010 to 2021.

Communications between senior executives, including Mark Zuckerberg, were "designed to mislead the public", Judge Mathew wrote in his order.

While the full amount of the penalty against Meta, based on thousands of violations of state law, was calculated as $219bn, Judge Mathew reduced the penalty to the $25bn fine.

It follows a $5bn fine levied by the US Federal Trade Commission in 2019 against the company over its data privacy practices.

Gaming_Tech.title: Tesla and SpaceX: Why does Elon Musk want to merge the companies?
Gaming_Tech.text:
Elon Musk has spent years building Tesla and SpaceX into a pair of trillion-dollar technology empires. Now, he is considering bringing them together.

Asked on Tuesday whether a merger would be a good idea, Musk was clear: "Yes."

The prospect is more than hypothetical. Musk said special committees have been formed to assess a potential deal, although he stressed that there is no guarantee a merger will happen and that nothing has been agreed.

With Tesla valued at roughly $1.5 trillion (£1.1 trillion) and SpaceX at $2 trillion, a combination of the two companies would mark the largest merger ever.

Any deal would also need shareholder backing. But Musk said he saw "a lot to be gained" in bringing the businesses together.

"In my opinion, 100%. It's just a question of when," says David Nicholson, chief technology advisor at market research firm The Futurum Group.

During Tesla's earnings call on Wednesday, Musk said he had nothing further to add about the prospect of a merger but quipped: "I feel like I'm tap-dancing through a minefield."

Musk said that calling the merger a certainty would be "overstating" things.

Tesla reported a slight drop in third quarter sales which came in at $28.05 billion compared with $28.1 billion at the same time last year.

The unveiling of the Tesla Roadster last week - a futuristic electric car powered by SpaceX rocket thrusters - served as a "symbolic embodiment" hinting at the two Musk companies merging, Nicholson said.

Musk, chief executive of both SpaceX and Tesla, said bringing the firms together would be beneficial given the work each does around chips, artificial intelligence (AI) and other technology projects.

Specifically, the deal would combine Tesla's cars, robots and self-driving technology with SpaceX's rockets, data centres, satellites and telecommunications operations.

The move could be a step towards Musk's mission to build a self-sustaining city on Mars - a vision that has invited sceptics but also plenty of backers.

Over the past year, Musk has moved to consolidate his businesses, with SpaceX acquiring xAI and X, formerly Twitter, before going public this year.

But the merger would ultimately be decided by shareholders, with half of Tesla's needed to back the deal, a threshold even Musk described as "quite a high hurdle".

Musk, as boss of both companies, cannot participate in shareholder discussions.

Even so, Musk, a key shareholder of Tesla, will likely get his way in the next few years, said investment analyst Dan Sheehan from Telos Wealth Advisors.

He believes shareholders will back the deal as the technology the companies develop complement each other, Sheehan said.

But the merger would mean that Tesla shareholders will likely hold a "smaller slice of a much larger and more complex business," he added.

"There's no real precedent for how a public company like Tesla gets priced in this," Sheehan said.

SpaceX shares rose 8% in after hours trading while shares of Tesla climbed by 2%.

Experts told the BBC that Tesla drivers are unlikely to see much drastic change in the near term, even if the two companies combine.

In fact, vehicles seem almost like "an afterthought", overshadowed by the potential to combine the Tesla and SpaceX's tech capabilities, Nicholson said.

Changes are already underway at Tesla. The carmaker said earlier this year that it would prioritise its best-selling Model Y and Model 3, shifting focus away from less popular models.

Tesla also started using a manufacturing plant in California to produce humanoid robots, known as Optimus.

However, the merger could attract scrutiny over Musk, already a polarising figure in the US, Nicholson said.

The move could also face more regulatory pressure if Democrats - many of whom have been critical of Musk - win more seats in the US midterm elections next month.

Shareholders have backed Musk's desires before. Last year, Tesla investors approved an unprecedented compensation package for Musk valued around $1tn.

"I honestly don't think Musk will be keeping track of what the merger will do for his wealth," Nicholson said.

The deal also brings Musk closer to what Nicholson says is "his mission in life": colonising Mars.

Gaming_Tech.title: Meta strikes deal to stop Mark Zuckerberg leaving California over billionaire tax
Gaming_Tech.text:
Meta has agreed a deal with Mark Zuckerberg to stop the Facebook co-founder from leaving California after he threatened to move from the state because of a proposed tax on billionaires.

The agreement allows Zuckerberg - reportedly one of the world's richest people - to sell shares in Meta without losing control of the Californian-based company if he needs to pay a large tax bill.

The measure, which would impose a one-time 5% tax on state residents with a net worth of more than $1bn (£750m), is yet to pass. Californian residents will vote on 3 November.

Nevertheless, Zuckerberg secured a deal with a special committee at Meta after "robust", and "at several points, contentious" negotiations.

California is home to most of the US's technology giants and there are around 225 billionaires who reside in the state, according to the Americans for Tax Fairness campaign group.

Zuckerberg - who has a $226bn fortune according to Forbes' billionaires tracker - had told Meta's board that it was his intention to remain with the firm for "the foreseeable future".

However, he said he was evaluating relocating his primary residence outside California and, if he listed his home on the real estate market, it "would be public and inevitably noted and commented upon by company employees".

This, he told the board, "would raise questions for management of the company going forward".

A special committee within Meta decided it was "critically important" to keep Zuckerberg in a leadership role and in California to manage the firm from its headquarters "during this era of unprecedented challenge and competition in our industry".

Tech companies in the US and globally are spending billions of dollars on developing artificial intelligence and the infrastructure around it.

Meta said the share deal was appropriate to ensure Zuckerberg "remains working closely" with the company's AI at its headquarters.

It said his "talent and leadership have been crucial to our growth, strategy, and stability since our inception, and the special committee wants that to continue".

Gaming_Tech.title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb
Gaming_Tech.text:
I once worked opposite a site where a shopping centre was being built.

We were warned there might be unexploded bombs from World War Two unearthed during the construction.

In the end, there were none, but procedures were put in place as a precaution and we all had to practice filing into designated safe zones inside our building.

The PHP story feels like the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb - I have never seen such a dramatic, public and global response to a cyber event that hasn't happened yet.

There has been no painful attack like the ransomware we saw knock out M&S and JLR in 2025.

But the potential threat is so serious that websites around the world have been taken down as a precaution.

Less than two months ago, 100 tech companies wrote an open letter warning the world to adopt a new level of cyber resilience in the age of AI.

It turns out we didn't have to wait very long to find out what they meant.

The weaknesses found in the PHP programming language, which is used by millions of websites, had been quietly resting there for years and are not easy to exploit.

One cyber security researcher told me he'd been up all night trying to do it as an experiment, but it was proving very difficult.

However, things that are very difficult for humans are increasingly very little trouble for AI.

The tech is getting a lot of credit here for assisting researchers in finding the bugs, and the PHP foundation, which oversees the programming language, was on the case and issued a fix.

It was supposed to be kept quiet until everyone had a chance to fix their sites - but the news was leaked.

From that point the clock started ticking.

As I write this, there are no reports that anyone or anything has succeeded in using the flaws to attack a site.

"There's a real dilemma," said Prof Alan Woodward from Surrey University.

"How do you alert people they need to be ready, and then that a patch is urgently required, whilst not alerting attackers?

"Basically you're telling everyone about the problem at the same time and hoping the defenders aren't awake enough to act as soon as the patch is out."

But we do know from large web companies like Cloudflare and Palo Alto Networks that millions of attempts have been made.

We probably won't know for a while whether it has worked for any criminals, because the companies affected might not be aware yet either.

As far as we know the unexploded bomb remains intact for now, and for some experts this is a success.

Gina Neff, Professor of Responsible AI at Queen Mary University, described this as a good news story.

"We've seen how a team of people supported by the large AI company have used AI to find the problem, work for months together to solve it and get everybody ready to be safe and secure," she told the Today Programme on BBC Radio 4.

"We have enormous capability to handle these risks."

But the baddies can use AI too, and those same tools are probably churning away right now trying to get in.

Cyber security authorities are warning website owners to fix the weaknesses immediately, but the patch only works on the latest version of PHP, so older sites will need to upgrade first.

For many it may be a significant repair job, so if there's a web developer in your life you may want to send them thoughts, prayers and maybe a strong coffee.

Gaming_Tech.title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning
Gaming_Tech.text:
The UK government says it is working to identify any potential exposure in its online services, after critical cyber-security flaws were identified in the PHP programming language that underpins a significant number of the world's websites.

Governments and some of the world's biggest companies are rushing to protect systems that use PHP before hackers can exploit the flaws.

The flaws were first discovered by AI, after which governments urged anyone who uses PHP to address them.

A UK government spokesperson urged "all organisations, private and public, large and small" to follow guidance to protect their systems.

The UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), as well as its counterparts in the EU and Australia, earlier urged those who use PHP to apply the fixes.

"Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated," the NCSC said in a statement., external

Amazon said its threat intelligence system identified it was targeted on Saturday. It added there were further "exploitation attempts" once the embargo on the flaw warning was lifted.

The company said it "automatically detected and restricted malicious scanning attempts targeting this vulnerability."

PHP powers a vast number of platforms, including online shops, Wikipedia and WordPress – the content management system behind many websites like blogs.

When you visit a website like Wikipedia, PHP is the code that collects information you need and presents it in a way you can read on the web.

Surrey Centre for Cyber Security Prof Alan Woodward said the flaw affects some 30 million websites.

As well as the scale of the flaw, Woodward said the nature of it means "an attacker can get their own code on to the webserver and run it and basically do whatever they like."

"They can steal data , they can go to other parts of your network. All sort of things like that - even plant a backdoor to get in later on, so it's pretty serious," Woodward told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.

Cyber security researcher Ryan Austin, who has been researching PHP security for the last 20 years, said he discovered the flaw in the programming language.

He told the Today programme it was "the most serious vulnerability I've ever found" which "started with a hunch that I would not have been able to scratch without AI".

Austin described PHP as "one of the first web languages that powered the early internet".

"It's in a lot of places that you wouldn't expect to be that are basically very core to how the internet runs in a lot of ways. It's like all the old things that are in a house that you know keeps it [running] but you don't really think about," the PHP researcher said.

But Austin said this incident is not necessarily bad news because organisations would now "run and patch PHP immediately" if they haven't already.

Amazon announced on Wednesday that it had identified a "PHP2Shell exploitation attempt" that occurred on 17 October.

In the attack, an anonymous internet address attempted to target weaknesses in one of Amazon's decoy or "honeypot" systems, the company's security chief CJ Moses said.

The use of an anonymous IP address suggests that the activity was conducted by a "threat actor", he said.

While the PHP Foundation intended to release its discovery later this month along with a complete fix for the problem, usually referred to by software developers as a "patch", details of the flaw were leaked on social media on Tuesday.

In subsequent attacks on Amazon that occurred on 21 October, "the actual payloads and choices in anonymisation infrastructure varied, suggesting these were multiple actors," Moses said.

The attacks occurred after the leak, but before the embargo was lifted on the PHP warning.

The use of AI means that "more actors can act within hours or even minutes once technical details of a vulnerability are disclosed", Moses added.

The PHP incident has "demonstrated how quickly AI is changing our cybersecurity landscape", Australian Council on AI Strategy CEO Anna-Maria Arabia told the BBC, as "what used to take months, to expose a vulnerability, is now taking days".

She warned that threats would only become more commonplace as AI technology rapidly improves. It is "not going backwards, in other words", she said.

The PHP flaws went undetected for at least a decade.

Cyber-security firm Wiz has estimated that "roughly 70%" of the internet is affected, though the BBC is unable to independently verify that figure.

The websites for several BBC programmes including Doctor Who and The Traitors are currently inaccessible.

They have not confirmed a link to PHP - BBC News has approached them for comment.

The Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) said it had followed guidance to take its website offline, "in view of the critical security issues affecting PHP".

Edinburgh and Oxford council websites also went offline on Wednesday, but are now accessible.

The Dutch cybersecurity agency went offline as a precaution, and Finland's government shut down its public web services. Wikipedia also took down parts of its website.

This was in line with advice issued by governments, including the US, to take websites down if the flaws could not immediately be fixed.

The US National Security Agency said that the vulnerabilities identified "often provide a direct path to the server's file system or database".

It could allow attackers to "steal sensitive data, disrupt services, or move deeper into a network. These vulnerabilities are flaws in PHP itself, not in the hosted application or its configuration," the NSA said in a later update.

OpenAI called the discovery, "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory".
